name: Boeing 787-10
sources: [787] Boeing D6-58333 Rev O (February 2023), 787 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/787.pdf. Overall length: 787-9 206 ft 1 in (62.81 m), p.2-6 (2.2.2); 787-10 224 ft 1 in (68.30 m), p.2-7 (2.2.3): 18 ft longer (5.49 m). The same on both (p.2-6, p.2-7): span 60.12 m, tailplane span 19.81 m, fuselage 5.77 m wide and 5.94 m tall, tail height 17.02 m, nose gear 5.41 m aft of the nose, track 9.80 m. Fuselage 62.00 m and 67.48 m: the tailplane tips end 0.81 m and 0.82 m aft of the tail cone.

Fuselage [787] p.2-16 (2.7.1 Door Locations), metres aft of the nose, 787-9 / 787-10: door 1 6.30 / 6.30; forward cargo door 11.00 / 11.00; door 2 18.36 / 21.41; door 3 35.43 / 38.48; aft cargo door 43.31 / 46.36; bulk cargo door 47.75 / 53.24; door 4 49.66 / 55.14. Door 2, door 3 and the aft cargo door, with the wing between them, are 10 ft (3.05 m) further aft; the bulk cargo door and door 4 are 18 ft (5.49 m) further aft. Thus the 787-10 has 3.05 m more ahead of the wing, between the forward cargo door and door 2, and 8 ft (2.44 m) more behind it, between the aft cargo door and the bulk cargo door. The same 3.05 m ahead of the wing: engine inlet 20.80 / 23.85 m aft of the nose, wheelbase 25.83 / 28.88 m (p.2-6, p.2-7). foreM + aftM = 5.49 m = 68.30 m - 62.81 m.

fore and aft: where the length goes in, metres aft of the base's nose on the base's mesh. Without them the tool works in the whole constant section each side of the wing, and door 2 comes out at 20.55 m and door 3 at 39.09 m (published 21.41 m and 38.48 m). The base's mesh is 65.79 m long against the document's 62.81 m (its fuselage skin is 62.82 m long, and its tailplane tips end 2.97 m behind the skin), and the tool puts the stations on it in proportion (x 1.047). fore: on the 787-9 the length goes in between the forward cargo door's aft edge (11.00 m + half of its 2.69 m opening, p.2-18: 12.35 m) and door 2's forward edge (18.36 m less half of a door 1.26 m wide, p.2-17: 17.73 m); a little inside, 12.4 to 17.7 m, which is 13.0 to 18.5 m on the mesh. The 787-8's recipe takes its 3.05 m out of the same stretch. aft: on the aircraft the length goes in behind the aft cargo door (aft edge 44.66 m) and ahead of the bulk cargo door (47.75 m less half of its 1.02 m cutout, p.2-19: 47.24 m). But the base's mesh has its aft cargo door (the recess on the right side, 40.27 to 42.97 m) 19.95 m behind the engine inlet lip (21.67 m), where the 787-8 has it (37.21 m - 17.76 m = 19.45 m). The 787-9 and the 787-10 have it 22.51 m behind the inlet (43.31 m - 20.80 m, 46.36 m - 23.85 m). So the length goes in ahead of the recess and behind door 3 (aft edge 37.8 m on the mesh): 38.0 to 40.2 m, which is 36.3 to 38.4 m on the document's length, between door 3 (35.43 m) and door 4 (49.66 m). The recess moves aft with the tail: 22.39 m behind the inlet lip. The wing-to-body fairing ends at 38.80 m and stays with the wing. The skin has no vertex between 33.9 m and 46.4 m, so the fuselage has the same shape wherever the length goes in behind the wing. Result on the document's length (68.30 m): doors 6.30, 21.41, 38.48 and 55.15 m (published 6.30, 21.41, 38.48 and 55.14 m).

Doors [787] p.2-16: four each side on both, the base's doors moved with the fuselage (door 1 not moved, doors 2 and 3 by the forward 3.05 m, door 4 by 5.49 m). The cockpit windows are on the nose section, which is the same. No stations of its own.

Wingtip and nacelles: no change. One wing with the same raked tips: span 60.12 m on both; the tip is 133 ft 6 in to 142 ft 3 in aft of the nose on the 787-9 (40.69 m and 43.36 m, p.2-6) and 143 ft 6 in to 152 ft 3 in on the 787-10 (p.2-7): 10 ft more, as door 2. p.2-7 prints 43.35 m and 47.01 m beside those feet, which are 43.74 m and 46.41 m; measured on its drawing (8.3 px/m): 43.8 m and 46.5 m. The same engines: 6.1.25 Inlet Hazard Areas, p.6-26, has one table for the General Electric engines and one for the Rolls Royce engines, for all models; the inlet is 10 ft further from the nose (20.80 / 23.85 m), as the wing. The engine centre line is labelled 32 ft 6 in (9.91 m) from the aircraft centre line on p.2-6 and 31 ft 10 in (9.71 m) on p.2-7. Measured on the two drawings it is 9.91 m (16.5 px/m) and 9.9 to 10.0 m (8.3 px/m): the same place, so the nacelles stay.

Gear [787] p.7-4 (7.2 Landing Gear Footprint): the same on the 787-9 and the 787-10 but for the wheelbase (84 ft 9 in and 94 ft 9 in): 4 wheels on each main leg, track 9.8 m, wheels 1.52 m apart across and axles 1.51 m apart, main tyres 54 x 21.0 R23, nose tyres 40 x 16.0 R16. No gear of its own: the tool adds the forward 3.05 m to the base's wheelbase (25.6 m: 28.65 m; published 25.83 m and 28.88 m). The base's clearance of 0.9 m holds: the nacelle is 0.74 to 0.99 m above the ground on the 787-10 (p.2-10, dimension F).
